title: Asana Review 2026: AI Teammates, Goals & The Best Project Management Tool for Teams?
content:
*Affiliate disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This never affects our ratings or recommendations. [Full disclosure](/disclosure)*

**Last updated: June 23, 2026**

## Quick Answer

**Asana** is a leading work management platform that helps teams coordinate projects, track goals, and automate workflows — all in one unified workspace. Trusted by over 170,000 organizations including Accenture, Figma, and Johnson & Johnson, Asana combines robust project management with AI-powered automation and real-time goal tracking. With a generous **Free plan** for individuals and small teams, paid plans starting at **$10.99/user/month** (Starter, billed annually), and advanced features like **AI Teammates**, **Portfolios**, and **Goal management**, Asana is one of the most complete project management solutions available in 2026. It's best for mid-to-large organizations that need structure, scalability, and cross-departmental visibility — though smaller teams may find the feature set overwhelming compared to simpler alternatives like Todoist or Notion.

---

## Pros and Cons

### Pros 👍

- **Industry-leading project management** — Multiple views (List, Board, Timeline, Calendar, Gantt) with drag-and-drop simplicity. Gantt-style Timeline view is one of the best in the category.
- **Powerful AI Teammates** — Asana's AI agents work alongside humans to automate task assignment, status updates, and workflow triggers. Available across Starter, Advanced, and Enterprise plans.
- **Goals & OKR tracking** — Built-in goal management with cascading objectives, progress tracking, and cross-portfolio alignment. No separate OKR tool needed.
- **Portfolio management** — See the big picture across all projects with real-time rollup reporting, resource allocation, and risk indicators.
- **Extensive integration library** — 300+ native integrations including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Workspace, Jira, Salesforce, Figma, and OpenAI connectors.
- **Workflow automation engine** — Create multi-step automated workflows (Rules) with triggers, conditions, and actions. No coding required.
- **Enterprise-grade security** — SOC 2 Type II, GDPR compliant, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, data export controls, and audit log.
- **G2 leader 2025** — Top 100 Best Software Products with 12,000+ reviews and 4.4/5 average rating.

### Cons 👎

- **Steep learning curve** — The feature richness can overwhelm new users. Expect 2-4 weeks for teams to fully adopt and integrate into daily workflows.
- **Expensive at scale** — Advanced plan at $24.99/user/month adds up fast for larger teams. Advanced features like Goals, Portfolios, and Time Tracking require the higher-tier Advanced plan.
- **No true offline mode** — Internet connection required for most functionality. The mobile app offers limited offline task viewing only.
- **Add-on pricing for extras** — AI Teammates and Timesheets & Budgets are separate add-ons, increasing the total cost beyond base subscription.
- **Notifications can be noisy** — Default settings generate high email and in-app notification volume. Requires deliberate configuration to avoid alert fatigue.

---

## Who Is Asana For?

**Ideal for:**
- **Mid-to-large companies** (50-500+ employees) managing complex cross-departmental projects
- **Marketing teams** coordinating campaigns, content calendars, and creative production
- **Operations teams** tracking strategic initiatives, OKRs, and resource planning
- **IT & Product teams** managing sprints, releases, and project intake
- **Agencies** juggling multiple client projects with portfolio-level oversight

**Not ideal for:**
- **Solo freelancers** — Notion or Todoist offer simpler, cheaper solutions for individual task management
- **Very small teams (2-5 people)** — The feature set may feel oversized; consider ClickUp or Monday.com for simpler onboarding
- **Teams needing native time tracking** — Timesheets is a paid add-on ($4.99/user/month); options like Toggl or Clockify integrate but add cost
- **Real-time chat-heavy teams** — Asana is not a Slack replacement. You'll still need a dedicated messaging tool for quick conversations

---

## Detailed Features Breakdown

### 1. Project Management & Views

Asana offers six project views that adapt to any workflow:

**List View** — The classic task list with columns for assignee, due date, status, and custom fields. Perfect for straightforward project tracking and daily task management. Supports drag-and-drop reordering, inline editing, and multi-level subtasks.

**Board View** — Kanban-style boards for visual workflow management. Ideal for content pipelines, product backlogs, and status-based tracking. Cards can be customized with cover images, custom fields, and dependencies.

**Timeline View** — Asana's flagship Gantt chart view. Visualize task dependencies, critical paths, and project schedules. Drag tasks to adjust dates, and see how delays ripple through dependent tasks. This is one of the strongest Gantt implementations among project management tools.

**Calendar View** — Traditional month/week/day view for deadline-oriented planning. Syncs with Google Calendar and Outlook. Tasks appear as calendar events with the ability to drag-and-drop reschedule.

**Goal View** — Track progress toward company-wide objectives. Set measurable goals with numeric targets, key results, and progress percentages. Goals cascade from company → department → individual, ensuring alignment across the organization.

**Portfolio View** — Aggregates multiple projects into a single dashboard. Monitor project health (on-track, at-risk, off-track), budget status, and resource allocation across your entire program portfolio.

### 2. AI Teammates & Automation

Asana's AI capabilities represent a significant 2026 update. The platform introduces **AI Teammates** — autonomous agents that work alongside human team members:

**Smart Assignment** — AI automatically assigns tasks based on workload, expertise, and past assignment patterns. Reduces manager overhead and ensures balanced distribution.

**AI Status Updates** — Generate weekly status reports automatically. The AI reviews task progress, completion rates, and blocked items to produce a narrative summary for stakeholders.

**Workflow Rules Engine** — Create automated triggers without code: "When a task moves to 'In Progress' AND has high priority → assign to reviewer AND set due date in 3 days AND notify Slack channel." Supports conditional logic, multi-step actions, and cross-project automation.

**AI Connectors** — Integration with OpenAI and other AI platforms allows teams to kick off projects and organize tasks directly from AI chat interactions. Turn conversations into structured work items.

**Smart Suggest** — As AI learns your team's patterns, it suggests task templates, workflow rules, and project structures based on historical data.

### 3. Goals & OKR Management

Asana's Goals module is built for strategic alignment:

- **Cascading goals** — Company → Department → Team → Individual alignment with visual hierarchy
- **Key Results tracking** — Set numeric targets (e.g., "Increase NPS from 72 to 85") with automatic progress calculation
- **Milestone tracking** — Define key dates and checkpoints for each objective
- **Portfolio integration** — See how projects roll up to strategic goals with automatic health indicators
- **Reporting dashboards** — Real-time goal progress reports with export capabilities for executive presentations

### 4. Integrations & Ecosystem

Asana connects with 300+ tools through native integrations and API:

**Communication:** Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, Outlook
**Productivity:** Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Dropbox, Box, OneDrive
**Developer:** GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Bitbucket, Linear
**Design:** Figma, Adobe Creative Cloud, Canva, Sketch
**CRM:** Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho CRM
**Marketing:** HubSpot, Marketo, Google Ads, Facebook Ads
**AI/ML:** OpenAI, ChatGPT, Claude, Zapier AI

The **Asana API** supports RESTful endpoints with webhooks for real-time event notifications. Rate limits are generous (150 requests per minute for most paid plans), making it suitable for custom integrations and automation.

### 5. Reporting & Dashboards

Asana provides robust reporting across all paid plans:

- **Dashboard** — Customizable widgets showing task completion, overdue items, workload distribution, and project health
- **Goals Dashboard** — Real-time OKR progress with visual indicators
- **Portfolio Dashboard** — Cross-project health with risk assessment
- **Workload view** — See who's over capacity across all projects (Advanced plan)
- **Custom reports** — Filter by custom fields, tags, assignees, due dates, and project
- **Export options** — CSV, PDF, and API access for custom data analysis

### 6. Mobile & Desktop Apps

**iOS & Android apps** — Full-featured mobile experience with task management, approvals, comments, and notification management. The mobile app supports offline viewing of cached tasks and updates sync when connectivity resumes. Push notifications for @mentions, task assignments, and deadline reminders.

**Desktop apps** — Native apps for Windows and macOS with support for system notifications, quick-add via global hotkey, and drag-and-drop file uploads.

---

## Pricing

| Plan | Price (Annual) | Price (Monthly) | Best For |
|------|---------------|-----------------|----------|
| **Personal** | Free | Free | 1-2 users managing personal tasks |
| **Starter** | $10.99/user/month | $13.49/user/month | Growing teams (3-50 users) |
| **Advanced** | $24.99/user/month | $30.49/user/month | Companies needing goals, portfolios, and workload |
| **Enterprise** | Custom pricing | Custom pricing | Large organizations with advanced security needs |
| **Enterprise+** | Custom pricing | Custom pricing | Mission-critical deployments with dedicated support |

### What's Included Per Plan

**Personal (Free):** Unlimited tasks, list/board/calendar views, basic search, mobile apps, collaborate with up to 10 collaborators, 100 MB storage per file.

**Starter:**
Everything in Personal, plus: Timeline (Gantt) view, workflow automation (Rules), 250+ app integrations, Asana AI (limited), forms for task intake, admin console, priority support, 1 GB storage per file.

**Advanced:**
Everything in Starter, plus: Goals & OKRs, Portfolios, Workload resource management, Time tracking (basic), custom templates, advanced reporting, approvals, custom branding, 5 GB storage per file.

**Enterprise:**
Everything in Advanced, plus: SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, data export controls, audit log API, advanced admin features, priority support with SLA, dedicated success manager, unlimited storage.

### Add-On Costs

- **AI Teammates** — Available on Starter, Advanced, Enterprise, and Enterprise+. Contact sales for pricing. (Not included in base subscription)
- **Timesheets & Budgets** — $4.99/user/month billed annually. Adds project budgets, timesheet entry, cost tracking, and profitability reporting.
- **Compliance management** — Custom pricing for regulated industries.

### Hidden Costs Analysis

The most significant cost consideration is the jump from Starter to Advanced. Goals, Portfolios, and Workload — features that differentiate Asana from lightweight alternatives — are locked behind the Advanced tier at $24.99/user/month. For a team of 20, that's **$499.80/month** compared to $219.80/month for Starter.

Additionally, the AI Teammates add-on is priced separately and not included in any plan tier. Organizations that want the full AI experience should budget 20-30% above the base subscription cost.

---

## Buyer's Guide: How to Choose the Right Asana Plan

**Step 1: Assess your team size and structure**
- 1-2 people doing personal projects → Personal (Free) is sufficient
- 3-15 people in a single department → Starter covers core needs
- 15+ people across multiple departments → Advanced or Enterprise

**Step 2: Identify your must-have features**
- Need Gantt charts? → Starter minimum (Timeline view)
- Need company-wide OKRs? → Advanced (Goals module)
- Need to see who's overworked? → Advanced (Workload)
- Need compliance/SAML/SSO? → Enterprise
- Need AI agents? → Starter + AI Teammates add-on

**Step 3: Calculate total cost with add-ons**
Don't just look at base pricing. If your team needs time tracking ($4.99/user/month) and AI Teammates, your real cost on Advanced could be $30-35/user/month.

**Step 4: Consider the migration effort**
Asana's data import supports CSV, Trello, Jira (CSV), and Monday.com (CSV). Allow 2-4 weeks for full team adoption. The free Personal plan lets you explore all core features before committing.

---

## Competitor Comparisons

### Asana vs ClickUp

ClickUp is Asana's most direct competitor and offers more features at a lower price point. ClickUp's Unlimited plan ($10/user/month) includes Gantt charts, goals, and whiteboards — features that require Asana's Advanced tier at $24.99/user/month.

**Where Asana wins:** Polish, reliability, and enterprise readiness. Asana rarely has bugs or downtime. The user interface is more intuitive and consistent than ClickUp's sprawling feature set.

**Where ClickUp wins:** Features-per-dollar ratio. ClickUp includes docs, whiteboards, email, and clip recording — all in one platform. Asana requires separate tools for many of these.

**Verdict:** Choose Asana for stability and enterprise needs. Choose ClickUp if you want maximum features on a budget.

### Asana vs Monday.com

Monday.com is a visual Work OS that emphasizes customizability over structure.

**Where Asana wins:** Goals/OKR tracking, Timeline (Gantt) view, and the AI Teammates ecosystem. Asana's goal cascading is more mature than Monday.com's objectives feature.

**Where Monday.com wins:** Visual flexibility, color-coded boards, and the "no-template" approach. Monday.com's boards feel more like a blank canvas, which creative teams love. The automation engine is also more visual and beginner-friendly.

**Verdict:** Choose Asana for structured project management with clear hierarchies. Choose Monday.com for visual, customizable workflows that need to flex across different use cases.

### Asana vs Notion

Notion has evolved from a note-taking app into a project management tool, but it approaches the category differently.

**Where Asana wins:** Project management fundamentals. Asana's task dependencies, timeline management, portfolio views, and workload tracking are vastly superior. Notion is a wiki that can look like a project manager; Asana IS a project manager.

**Where Notion wins:** Flexibility and documentation. Notion's databases, wikis, and document editor create a unified knowledge base. For teams that need project management AND documentation in one tool, Notion is compelling.

**Verdict:** Choose Asana for dedicated, structured project management. Choose Notion if you need an all-in-one wiki + light project management tool.

### Asana vs Jira

Jira (by Atlassian) is the gold standard for software development teams.

**Where Asana wins:** Usability for non-technical teams. Marketing, operations, HR, and creative teams find Asana intuitive. Jira's technical jargon (epics, stories, sprints, points) alienates non-developers.

**Where Jira wins:** Software development workflows. Jira's sprint planning, backlog management, story points, and DevOps integrations are unmatched.

**Verdict:** Choose Asana for cross-organizational work management. Choose Jira for software development specifically. Many enterprises use both (Jira for engineering, Asana for the rest of the business).

### Asana vs Trello

Trello (also Atlassian) is the simplest project management tool on the market.

**Where Asana wins:** Depth. Asana's feature set makes Trello look like a child's toy — Timeline, Goals, Portfolios, Workload, AI, and 300+ integrations vs Trello's single-board view with Power-Ups.

**Where Trello wins:** Simplicity and speed. You can set up Trello in 5 minutes and teach it in 2. For very simple workflow tracking (e.g., "To Do → Doing → Done"), Trello is faster and cheaper.

**Verdict:** Choose Asana for serious team project management. Choose Trello for simple personal or small-team Kanban workflows.

Asana has also been recognized as a **Leader in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Collaborative Work Management** for three consecutive years, positioning it alongside Microsoft and Atlassian in the leaders' quadrant.

---

## Tips for Getting the Most Out of Asana

1. **Start with templates, not from scratch.** Asana has 100+ pre-built project templates for common workflows (campaign management, product launch, onboarding, etc.). Using them accelerates adoption by 40-60%.

2. **Configure notifications on day one.** Default notification settings are aggressive. Spend 15 minutes per user setting up personal notification preferences to avoid alert fatigue. Key settings: disable email notifications for task assignments you already see in-app, enable Slack notifications for @mentions only.

3. **Use Rules before buying automations.** The free-tier Rules engine handles 80% of common automation needs (auto-assign, status changes, due date reminders). Don't pay for complex automation tools until you've maxed out Asana's built-in Rules.

4. **Create a project intake form.** Starter plan and above include Forms — embeddable task intake forms that create tasks automatically. This single feature eliminates the "send me an email about it" problem and centralizes all incoming requests.

5. **Leverage the Portfolio view monthly.** For managers overseeing 5+ projects, the Portfolio view provides a 5-minute executive summary if your team keeps status fields updated. Make it a weekly habit to review and update project status.

6. **Adopt the Goals module gradually.** Start with 3-5 company-level OKRs for one quarter before cascading to departments. Trying to do full OKR implementation in one sprint overwhelms teams and leads to abandoned goal tracking.

7. **Integrate with your communication tool first.** The Slack or Teams integration is the single highest-ROI integration. It turns messages into tasks without switching apps. Configure the integration before any others.

---

## FAQ

### What is Asana and how does it work?

Asana is a work management platform that helps teams organize, track, and manage their work. It works through projects, tasks, and goals — users create projects, break them into tasks with assignees and due dates, and track progress through various views (list, board, timeline, calendar). The platform also includes AI Teammates for automation, Goals for OKR tracking, and Portfolios for cross-project visibility.

### Does Asana have a free plan?

Yes. Asana's Personal plan is free forever and includes unlimited tasks, list/board/calendar views, basic search, mobile apps, collaboration with up to 10 guests, and 100 MB file storage. It's suitable for individuals and very small teams managing personal projects.

### How much does Asana cost per month?

Asana's paid plans start at $10.99/user/month billed annually for Starter ($13.49/month billed monthly) and $24.99/user/month billed annually for Advanced ($30.49/month billed monthly). Enterprise and Enterprise+ plans have custom pricing. Optional add-ons include AI Teammates (custom pricing) and Timesheets & Budgets ($4.99/user/month).

### Does Asana include AI features?

Yes. Asana offers AI Teammates as an add-on across Starter, Advanced, Enterprise, and Enterprise+ plans. AI capabilities include smart task assignment, automated status updates, intelligent workflow suggestions, and AI connectors that let teams create projects from AI chat interactions (OpenAI, etc.).

### Is Asana better than Monday.com?

Asana excels at structured project management with industry-leading Timeline (Gantt) view, Goals/OKR tracking, and Portfolio management. Monday.com offers more visual customization and a simpler automation builder. For organizations that prioritize structure, goals alignment, and enterprise readiness, Asana is generally the better choice. For teams that want visual flexibility and creative workflows, Monday.com may be a better fit.

### Does Asana integrate with Slack?

Yes. Asana has a deep native integration with Slack. You can create tasks from Slack messages, receive Asana notifications in Slack channels, attach Slack conversations to tasks, and share task updates directly to Slack. This is one of Asana's most popular integrations.

### Can Asana replace Jira for software teams?

For basic software project tracking, Asana can work — but it's not a Jira replacement. Jira offers specialized features for software development: sprint planning, backlog management, story points, velocity tracking, and deep CI/CD integrations. Many organizations use Asana for cross-departmental work management while keeping Jira for engineering teams specifically.

### How secure is Asana?

Asana maintains SOC 2 Type II certification and is GDPR compliant. Enterprise plans include SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, data export controls, audit log API, and encrypted data at rest and in transit. Asana has completed third-party penetration testing and maintains a bug bounty program. They publish a transparency report and detailed security documentation.

### Does Asana have a mobile app?

Yes. Asana offers full-featured mobile apps for both iOS and Android. The mobile apps support task management, approvals, comments, file uploads, and notification management. There is limited offline support (cached tasks can be viewed without internet). The mobile app has a 4.5/5 rating on the App Store and 4.3/5 on Google Play.

### What's the difference between Starter and Advanced plans?

Starter ($10.99/user/month) includes Timeline view, workflow automation (Rules), 250+ app integrations, forms, and limited Asana AI. Advanced ($24.99/user/month) adds Goals & OKRs, Portfolios, Workload resource management, time tracking, custom templates, advanced reporting, approvals, and custom branding. The key difference is that Advanced unlocks the strategic layer — goals, portfolios, and workload management that connect individual projects to company objectives.

### Can I import data from Trello or Monday.com?

Yes. Asana supports data import from Trello, Monday.com, Jira, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, and CSV/Excel files. The import process maps boards and cards to Asana projects and tasks. For complex imports, Asana's support team can assist with migration.

---

## Conclusion

Asana has earned its position as one of the most comprehensive and reliable project management platforms on the market. Its combination of robust project views, industry-leading Timeline (Gantt) implementation, strategic Goals and Portfolio management, and increasingly capable AI features make it a strong choice for organizations that take project management seriously.

The platform excels in structured environments where cross-departmental visibility and goal alignment matter. For mid-to-large companies with clear hierarchies and defined workflows, Asana delivers exceptional value — albeit at a higher price point than many competitors.

**Who should buy Asana today:**
- Teams of 10+ that need Gantt charts, goal tracking, and portfolio visibility
- Organizations adopting or refining OKR practices
- Enterprises that need SOC 2 compliance and enterprise-grade security
- Marketing, operations, and product teams managing complex cross-functional projects

**Who should consider alternatives:**
- Freelancers and very small teams — Notion or Todoist are simpler and cheaper
- Budget-conscious organizations — ClickUp offers more features at a lower price
- Software development teams — Jira remains the specialized tool for engineering
- Teams that prioritize visual customization — Monday.com offers more design flexibility

**Ready to try Asana?** Start with the Free Personal plan to explore the interface, then upgrade to Starter ($10.99/user/month) when your team needs Gantt charts and automation. If your organization needs goals, portfolios, and workload management, the Advanced plan ($24.99/user/month) is worth the investment. [Try Asana Free →](https://asana.com/)
